dossier.public_summary: The dip is deep (~1.6%, 13-15 Earth radii), V-shaped, very grazing and much shorter than a central planet transit around this M dwarf should be. It sits on the target star and the star shows signs of binarity. The depth also changes by ~43% between sectors in a pattern not explained by calibration, which together positively favours a small grazing eclipsing binary on the target over a planet.

reasons.why: Very high V-shape with long ingress (best_ingress_fraction 0.4, b 0.8698) favours grazing eclipsing binary / stellar eclipse, not a flat-bottomed planet transit.
Observed duration (0.9889 h) is about half the central duration expected for the M-dwarf (1.849 h), consistent with the stellar-density penalty (9.657) and a non-planetary eclipse shape.
Undiluted depth 18620 ppm and rp/rstar 0.1365 give 13.24–15.05 Rearth, well above 10 Rearth planet regime into giant-planet / small-star regime; a planet that large at this short period is unlikely.
Large Gaia RUWE indicates the star is an astrometric binary; combined with high excess noise and variable dip, points to an eclipsing binary on the target.

Depth changes 43.09% between sectors (19532, 16429, 12562 ppm). Tool reports changes_within_a_source (verdict changes_within_a_source, p 9.375e-30 between TESS-SPOC sectors, p_consistent 1.45e-48 between individual transits), indicating real astrophysical change, not calibration.
On-target centroid (offset 0.6065 arcsec, 0.5884 sigma) rules out neighbour eclipses (plausible_within_1px 0, could_cause_within_1px 0), leaving EB on target as best explanation.
